It separately prohibits 'lotteries, auctions, contests, sweepstakes, or games of chance', 'Betting-related products, competition/event tickets, or entries', fantasy sports, money transfer services, and marketplaces. Paddle does run a 'Paddle for games' product, but for game and DLC licences, not in-game currency.

checklist.item: Paddle / merchant-of-record for the SUBSCRIPTION only (Model D)
checklist.issuer: Paddle, FastSpring, Polar or similar MoR
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED (Paddle's published headline is a percentage-plus-fixed reseller fee; confirm current rate card)
checklist.prerequisite: Legal entity, tax residency declaration
checklist.notes: A recurring fee for features and cosmetics with no stake and no prize is squarely inside every MoR's acceptable use. This is the only model where the MoR route is clean.

checklist.item: Understand precisely what merchant-of-record does and does not move
checklist.issuer: Internal / counsel
checklist.prerequisite: none
checklist.notes: MoR MOVES: the card-scheme merchant relationship and chargeback liability; PCI-DSS merchant scope (the MoR hosts checkout); sales-tax/VAT/GST registration, collection, remittance and invoicing in ~100 jurisdictions; the consumer-contract counterparty and refund obligation. MoR DOES NOT MOVE: gambling or gaming licensing — the licensable act is OFFERING the game, which is you, not the reseller; money transmission — if you hold a user balance and pay it out, that is your activity and no MoR touches it; KYC/AML on payouts; age assurance inside the game; the underlying legality of the stake. Decisive practical point: MoRs are a ONE-WAY pay-in rail. None of Paddle, FastSpring or Lemon Squeezy does player payouts. For Models B and C the payout half — the hard, regulated half — is entirely unserved by MoR.

checklist.item: PayPal / Braintree — treat as unavailable for B and C without explicit pre-approval
checklist.issuer: PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. / PayPal, Inc. / Braintree
checklist.prerequisite: Pre-approval; demonstrated ability to block gambling for US account holders and any jurisdiction where it may be illegal
checklist.notes: PayPal's Acceptable Use Policy prohibits gambling — 'placing, accepting, recording, or registering bets... or otherwise carrying on a game of chance for money, property, or other things of value' — absent pre-approval, and PayPal's help content states approval requires satisfying PayPal that you can block US account holders. Secondary sources (SeamlessChex, July 2026) report holding a recognised gaming licence does not by itself lift the restriction. PayPal is fine for Models A and D as ordinary digital goods.

checklist.item: Gambling-specialist acquirer / PSP (licence-gated)
checklist.issuer: Worldpay (FIS), Nuvei, Paysafe (Skrill/Neteller), Trustly, PayNearMe, Praxis Tech — vendor list is indicative, from trade knowledge not a fetched source
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED — expect a markedly higher discount rate than 2.9%, a rolling reserve, and a minimum monthly volume
checklist.prerequisite: Gambling/gaming licence in each market; MCC 7995 registration; card-network high-integrity-risk programme registration
checklist.notes: This is the only realistic rail for a cash-redeemable stake product. Every one of them requires the licence first, so the payments workstream cannot start until the licensing workstream is finished. UNVERIFIED: MCC 7995 assignment rules and Visa/Mastercard high-integrity-risk registration fees were not verified in this research — confirm with the acquirer.

checklist.item: Apple: use StoreKit in-app purchase for coin sales in Model A and subscriptions in Model D
checklist.issuer: Apple
checklist.cost: Apple commission — UNVERIFIED current rate card (standard and Small Business Program rates were not fetched)
checklist.prerequisite: Apple Developer Program membership
checklist.notes: App Store Review Guideline 3.1.1 requires IAP to unlock 'in-game currencies'. Two traps: (a) 'Any credits or in-game currencies purchased via in-app purchase may not expire' — so coin balances cannot be time-expired; (b) if you ever ship randomised rewards, 3.1.1 requires disclosing the odds of each item type before purchase.

checklist.item: Apple: Model B cannot sell its stake currency through IAP — this is a hard block, not a review-risk
checklist.issuer: Apple App Store Review
checklist.prerequisite: none
checklist.notes: Guideline 5.3.3 verbatim: 'Apps may not use in-app purchase to purchase credit or currency for use in conjunction with real money gaming of any kind.' Guideline 5.3.4: real-money-gaming apps 'must have necessary licensing and permissions in the locations where the app is used, must be geo-restricted to those locations, and must be free on the App Store.' Combined effect: on iOS a Model B app must be free, licensed, geofenced, and must fund balances OUTSIDE IAP via a web top-up. Note the historic Guideline 4.7.1 real-money-gaming restriction has been removed and 4.7 now covers mini apps, mini games and emulators — do not rely on stale 4.7 advice.

checklist.item: Apple: if Model B or C funds balances off-app, build the web top-up flow and rely on the US-storefront link-out carve-out
checklist.issuer: Apple
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED (US external-link commission rate not fetched)
checklist.prerequisite: Apple Developer Program; for non-US storefronts, a StoreKit External Purchase Link Entitlement
checklist.notes: Guideline 3.1.1(a) now states entitlements 'are not required for developers to include buttons, external links, or other calls to action in their United States storefront apps', and that the anti-steering prohibition applies 'In all other storefronts, except for the United States storefront, where this prohibition does not apply'. So a US-storefront app may link out to a web wallet top-up freely; EU and other storefronts need the External Purchase Link Entitlement. India follows the general rule.

checklist.item: Google Play: complete the gambling-app application and hold a licence per country/state for Model B
checklist.issuer: Google Play
checklist.prerequisite: Approved governmental operator status or registration as a licensed operator with the appropriate gambling authority, plus a valid operating licence in each specified country
checklist.notes: Play's Real-Money Gambling, Games, and Contests policy requires the app be free to download, NOT use Google Play In-app Billing, prevent under-age users, geo-block countries/states not covered by the licence, be rated AO (Adult Only) or IARC equivalent, and display responsible-gambling information. Unlicensed apps that let users 'wager, stake, or participate using real money... to obtain a prize of real world monetary value' are prohibited outright. Secondary reporting (Lexology, igamingexpert 2025) indicates Google tightened its treatment of sweepstakes and dual-currency models and now treats virtual currencies or items with real-world value as gambling.

checklist.item: Google Play: use Google Play Billing for Model A coins and Model D subscriptions
checklist.issuer: Google Play
checklist.cost: Service fee — UNVERIFIED base rate; India and South Korea alternative billing carries a 4-percentage-point reduction per the Payments policy
checklist.prerequisite: Play Console account
checklist.notes: Play's Payments policy requires Play billing for 'Digital items (such as virtual currencies, extra lives, additional playtime, add-on items, characters, or avatars)'. Alternative billing exists in three flavours: India/South Korea (user-choice billing, 4% fee reduction); EEA (alternative billing in-app plus permission to direct users outside the app to promote offers); United States (additional alternative billing options and lead-out to external content, per the District Court order in Epic v. Google, for enrolled developers). Note the tension: Play requires Play Billing for virtual currency in a normal game, but FORBIDS Play Billing in a licensed real-money gambling app — the two policies do not compose, which is itself the signal that Model B is not a Play-native product.

checklist.item: India: assume NO payment rail exists for Models B or C and do not attempt to build one
checklist.issuer: MeitY / RBI / NPCI / Indian banks and payment aggregators
checklist.prerequisite: none
checklist.notes: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 (Act No. 32 of 2025, assent 22 August 2025) prohibits all online money games whether of chance, of skill, or a combination, and — per multiple law-firm summaries (Trilegal; PIB press releases) — a dedicated section bars banks, financial institutions and 'any other person facilitating financial transactions' including payment aggregators, gateways, wallet operators and card networks from facilitating any transaction toward payment for an online money gaming service. The section number is reported as section 7 in secondary sources; UNVERIFIED — the statutory text could not be fetched (meity.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in returned 403). The Rules were notified 22 April 2026 (Wikipedia, secondary). Practical consequence for the payments lane: a payment aggregator, not just you, commits an offence, so no Indian PA will onboard the merchant at any price.

checklist.item: India: Models A and D route through a normal RBI-authorised payment aggregator
checklist.issuer: Razorpay, Cashfree, PayU or similar RBI-authorised PA
checklist.prerequisite: Indian entity or cross-border arrangement; PA merchant onboarding KYC
checklist.notes: The 2025 Act carves out and promotes 'online social games' and e-sports. A closed-loop cosmetic coin and a subscription are social-game monetisation, not money gaming. UNVERIFIED: the RBI Payment Aggregator directions' current merchant-onboarding and prohibited-category text was not fetched (search budget exhausted). Confirm with the PA that a non-redeemable in-game coin is acceptable under their category list and that they are comfortable post-Act.

checklist.item: FinCEN MSB registration (Form 107) as a money transmitter
checklist.issuer: FinCEN (US Treasury)
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED (registration itself is not fee-bearing; the AML programme cost is the real cost)
checklist.leadTime: Registration due within 180 days of the date the business is established; renewal every two years — UNVERIFIED, confirm against 31 CFR 1022.380
checklist.prerequisite: Legal entity; written AML programme; designated compliance officer
checklist.notes: The trigger is FinCEN guidance FIN-2013-G001 (18 March 2013). 'Convertible virtual currency' is virtual currency that 'either has an equivalent value in real currency, or acts as a substitute for real currency'. An 'administrator' is 'a person engaged as a business in issuing (putting into circulation) a virtual currency, and who has the authority to redeem (to withdraw from circulation) such virtual currency' — and an administrator of a CVC is a money transmitter. The moment FACT//DUEL coins are redeemable for cash, the coins become CVC and the company becomes an administrator. Conversely: 'A user who obtains convertible virtual currency and uses it to purchase real or virtual goods or services is not an MSB' — which is exactly Model A, where the coin has no real-currency equivalent and cannot substitute for currency.

checklist.item: Written BSA/AML programme, designated compliance officer, independent testing, training
checklist.issuer: FinCEN (31 CFR 1022.210)
checklist.prerequisite: MSB status determination
checklist.notes: Note an important structural point: 31 CFR 1010.100(t) defines a BSA 'casino' as an establishment 'duly licensed or authorized to do business as such in the United States' with 'gross annual gaming revenue in excess of $1 million'. An unlicensed sweepstakes-model operator therefore is NOT a BSA casino and does not get the casino rules — it falls into the MSB money-transmitter regime instead, which is the stricter, lower-threshold one.

checklist.item: SAR filing capability
checklist.issuer: FinCEN
checklist.leadTime: Must file no later than 30 calendar days after initial detection
checklist.prerequisite: AML programme; transaction monitoring
checklist.notes: 31 CFR 1022.320: an MSB must report a suspicious transaction that 'involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least $2,000'; file 'no later than 30 calendar days after the date of the initial detection'; and 'maintain a copy of any SAR filed and the original or business record equivalent of any supporting documentation for a period of five years from the date of filing the SAR'. Note the $2,000 SAR floor is far below the $10,000 CTR floor — SARs, not CTRs, will be the operative burden for a consumer game.

checklist.item: CTR filing capability for cash-equivalent aggregation over $10,000/day
checklist.issuer: FinCEN
checklist.prerequisite: AML programme
checklist.notes: UNVERIFIED — 31 CFR 1010.311/1010.306 were not fetched in this research (eCFR blocked). The $10,000 currency-transaction threshold is well established but confirm applicability: CTRs attach to CURRENCY, and a card-funded online game may have little or no currency activity. Do not build CTR machinery before counsel confirms it is in scope.

checklist.item: State money transmitter licences (MTLs)
checklist.issuer: State banking departments via NMLS; model law is the CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED per state — surety bond, minimum net worth and permissible-investment requirements apply under the MTMA framework
checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — historically many months to years for a 40+ state footprint
checklist.prerequisite: FinCEN registration; audited financials; surety bonds; fingerprinting of control persons
checklist.notes: The MTMA is enacted in whole or part in 31 states per CSBS (secondary). Two carve-outs matter enormously here: the MTMA defines 'money' to EXCLUDE virtual currency, and the virtual-currency definition itself excludes certain merchant-rewards value and game-platform value (secondary — Virginia MTMA analysis; Virginia's Act is effective 1 July 2026). Only North Dakota and Minnesota have enacted the optional virtual-currency provisions (secondary). UNVERIFIED: the exact MTMA statutory text of the game-platform exclusion was not fetched. This carve-out is the single most valuable thing for counsel to confirm, because if a non-redeemable game coin sits inside it, Model A is unlicensable-free in every MTMA state and Model B's exposure turns entirely on the redeemability.

checklist.item: Identity verification vendor for any account that can receive a payout
checklist.issuer: Stripe Identity, Persona, Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido (Entrust), Jumio
checklist.cost: Stripe Identity VERIFIED at $1.50 per document-and-selfie verification and $0.50 per ID-number lookup (US SSN only), from stripe.com/pricing fetched 14 Sep 2026. Persona, Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido and Jumio list prices are UNVERIFIED — only low-quality comparison-blog sources were reachable, which put the range at roughly $0.80-$5.00 per check with annual enterprise contracts from ~$50k. Treat as indicative only.
checklist.leadTime: Days for self-serve (Stripe Identity, Veriff); weeks for enterprise contracts
checklist.prerequisite: Privacy notice covering biometric processing; DPA; retention schedule
checklist.notes: Verify at FIRST PAYOUT, not at signup — verifying every registrant destroys the funnel and creates needless biometric-data liability. Practical split: Stripe Identity if you are already on Stripe for Model A/D; Persona or Sumsub if you need configurable workflows plus PEP/sanctions screening in one vendor; Sumsub and Veriff are the usual iGaming choices. Biometric selfie matching triggers Illinois BIPA and Texas CUBI — get a written consent flow and do not store templates longer than needed.

checklist.item: Sanctions and PEP screening at onboarding and on an ongoing basis
checklist.issuer: OFAC (US), EU consolidated list, UN
checklist.cost: Usually bundled with the IDV vendor; UNVERIFIED standalone
checklist.prerequisite: IDV vendor selection
checklist.notes: OFAC obligations are strict-liability and apply to ALL models the moment you pay anyone money, including a Model C prize winner. There is no de minimis. Geo-blocking by IP alone is not a sanctions programme.

checklist.item: Age assurance: consume the App Store / Play age signal and gate real-money features
checklist.issuer: Texas, Utah and Louisiana App Store Accountability Acts
checklist.prerequisite: App-store SDK integration
checklist.notes: Texas: effective 1 Jan 2026; a preliminary injunction was stayed by the Fifth Circuit (Morrison Foerster, Nov 2025) so the law is operative. Utah: developer and provider obligations 6 May 2026, private right of action 31 Dec 2026. Louisiana: 1 July 2026. The stores verify age at account creation and bracket users as under-13, 13-15, 16-17 and 18+, and must obtain parental consent for downloads, app purchases and IN-APP PURCHASES. The developer-side duty is to receive that signal and act on it. This applies to Model A and D too — a minor's coin purchase needs parental consent in those states.

checklist.item: Independent age verification for any real-money feature (not just the store signal)
checklist.issuer: State gambling regulators; UK Gambling Commission and Ofcom as the near-neighbour benchmark
checklist.cost: Per-check IDV cost, see IDV line
checklist.prerequisite: IDV vendor
checklist.notes: UNVERIFIED — the UK Online Safety Act 2023 'highly effective age assurance' duties and their commencement date could not be verified in this research (ofcom.org.uk returned 403). The widely reported position is that HEAA duties for pornographic and other primary-priority content commenced 25 July 2025 and that licensed gambling is regulated by the Gambling Commission's LCCP rather than the OSA. Verify both with UK counsel before relying on either. EU: the DSA Article 28 minor-protection duties and the Commission's 2025 guidelines are the relevant instrument — also UNVERIFIED here.

checklist.item: W-9 collection from US payees and W-8BEN from non-US payees before any payout
checklist.issuer: IRS
checklist.prerequisite: Payout flow
checklist.notes: Collect the TIN BEFORE the money moves, not at year end. Missing TIN triggers 24% backup withholding, which you cannot recover from the user after the fact.

checklist.item: Form 1099-MISC for non-wagering contest prizes
checklist.issuer: IRS
checklist.appliesTo: C (and B if structured as a non-wagering sweepstakes)
checklist.prerequisite: W-9 on file
checklist.notes: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act the 1099-MISC reporting threshold rises from $600 to $2,000 for payments made from 2026, inflation-indexed from 2027 (secondary: Avalara, OnPay, Patriot Software — the statutory section was not fetched). Prizes and awards from a non-wagering skill contest go in Box 3 'Other income', not on Form W-2G. The IRS Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754 (rev. 01/2026) cover gambling winnings only and do not address skill contests — confirm the characterisation with tax counsel, because it turns on whether the entry fee is a 'wager'.

checklist.item: Form W-2G for wagering winnings
checklist.issuer: IRS
checklist.leadTime: Annual; statement to winner at time of payment
checklist.prerequisite: W-9 on file; withholding capability
checklist.notes: From Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754 (rev. 01/2026), fetched 14 Sep 2026: for sweepstakes, wagering pools and lotteries, report when winnings meet or exceed the applicable reporting threshold AND are at least 300 times the wager; regular gambling withholding of 24% applies when winnings minus the wager exceed $5,000; backup withholding of 24% applies where regular withholding does not and no TIN is supplied. The bingo/slot threshold rose from $1,200 to $2,000 effective 1 January 2026 and thresholds are now annually inflation-indexed under OBBBA (secondary: Holland & Knight, RSM, Baker Tilly). The 300x rule is decisive for a duel game: a $1 stake winning $100 is 100x and falls below it; a $1 stake winning $2,000 does not.

checklist.item: Form 1099-K awareness if you ever become a third-party settlement organisation
checklist.issuer: IRS
checklist.prerequisite: Determination that you are a TPSO
checklist.notes: OBBBA restored the 1099-K threshold to gross payments exceeding $20,000 AND more than 200 transactions, retroactive to 2022, replacing the $2,500 and $600 phase-ins (secondary: Avalara, TurboTax, Patriot Software). This most likely lands on your PSP rather than on you — but if you settle player-to-player value you may be the TPSO. Confirm with counsel.

checklist.item: Unclaimed property / escheatment programme for abandoned user balances
checklist.issuer: State unclaimed-property administrators (NAUPA); most states on a version of RUUPA
checklist.appliesTo: B, C (and A only if the coin is ever refundable to cash)
checklist.leadTime: Annual reporting cycle; dormancy typically 1-5 years depending on state
checklist.prerequisite: Balance ledger with last-activity timestamps per user; due-diligence letter capability
checklist.notes: This is the obligation founders miss. A cash-redeemable balance sitting in a dormant account is unclaimed property. Colorado's RUUPA expressly covers stored-value cards including the unused monetary value held by the issuer (secondary: Baker Tilly, EisnerAmper, NAUPA). There is no uniform rule — a state-by-state analysis is required. Two structural facts to raise with counsel: (a) priority is generally to the state of the owner's last known address, falling back to the holder's STATE OF INCORPORATION, so Delaware incorporation pulls all address-unknown balances into Delaware's regime (this priority rule was not verified in this research — flag as UNVERIFIED); (b) a coin that is genuinely non-redeemable in Model A is arguably not 'property' at all, which is another reason the closed-loop design is worth preserving. Design implication: record last-activity timestamps and never silently zero a balance.

checklist.item: PCI-DSS SAQ A via hosted fields or a hosted checkout
checklist.issuer: PCI Security Standards Council; acquirer enforces
checklist.cost: $0 for self-assessment; ASV quarterly scan cost UNVERIFIED
checklist.prerequisite: Never let card data touch your DOM or servers
checklist.notes: Use Stripe Elements, Adyen Drop-in/Components or an equivalent iframe/hosted-field integration and you qualify for SAQ A rather than SAQ A-EP or D. Under PCI DSS v4.0.1, effective 1 April 2025, the SAQ A eligibility criteria now require the merchant to confirm its site 'is not susceptible to attacks from scripts that could affect the merchant's e-commerce system(s)'. Requirements 6.4.3 (authorise and assure integrity of every script on the payment page) and 11.6.1 (change-and-tamper detection on the payment page) were removed from the SAQ A checklist itself but are named as the techniques by which you demonstrate eligibility. FACT//DUEL is a heavily scripted React/three.js app — the page hosting the payment iframe is precisely what Magecart-style attacks target, so script inventory, SRI and CSP are load-bearing here, not optional. If you build your own card form you drop to SAQ A-EP and the burden multiplies.

checklist.item: Separate the money ledger from the game ledger in the data model before any of this
checklist.issuer: Internal architecture
checklist.leadTime: Design decision — cheapest now, very expensive later
checklist.prerequisite: none
checklist.notes: Today all profile state is in IndexedDB with no server identity. Whatever model is chosen, keep three ledgers physically distinct: (1) purchased value, (2) earned/granted value, (3) prize/withdrawable value. Never let them commingle into one 'coins' integer. Regulators, processors and auditors all ask the same question — 'can purchased value become withdrawable value?' — and a single-integer wallet cannot answer 'no'. Dual-currency separation is also the only way to keep Model A defensible if you later bolt on a sweepstakes tier.

checklist.item: EU: determine whether you need an EMI or payment institution authorisation, or fit the limited network exclusion
checklist.issuer: National competent authority (e.g. DNB, BaFin, CBI, CSSF); EBA guidelines on the limited network exclusion
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED — EMI initial capital and application fees vary by member state
checklist.prerequisite: EU entity; governance, capital and safeguarding arrangements
checklist.notes: PSD2 Article 3(k) excludes payment instruments usable only in a limited way; secondary commentary is consistent that the exclusion requires NO CASH-OUT, which maps exactly onto the Model A / Model B dividing line. If coins can be converted back to money, you are issuing e-money or providing a payment service and need authorisation plus safeguarding of customer funds. UNVERIFIED: the EBA Guidelines text and the LNE notification thresholds were not fetched. Note the regime is changing — PSD3 and the PSR reportedly reached provisional political agreement on 27 November 2025 and would merge the PI and EMI regimes into one licence, with application around 2027 (secondary, UNVERIFIED). Apply under PSD2/EMD2 now; expect grandfathering.

checklist.item: EU: AML obligations as a provider of gambling services
checklist.issuer: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR); AMLA; national FIUs
checklist.appliesTo: B, C (if characterised as gambling in the member state)
checklist.prerequisite: Member-state gambling characterisation
checklist.notes: UNVERIFIED — eur-lex.europa.eu was unreachable from this environment across four attempts, so no article number or EUR threshold from AMLR 2024/1624 is asserted here. What counsel must pin down: (1) the article listing providers of gambling services as obliged entities; (2) the CDD trigger threshold for wagering a stake and for collecting winnings; (3) whether the member state has exercised any low-risk exemption; (4) the AMLR application date. Do not act on remembered figures for any of these.

checklist.item: Payout rail selection (this is a separate procurement from the pay-in rail)
checklist.issuer: Stripe Connect, PayPal Payouts/Hyperwallet, Trolley, Tremendous, Tango Card
checklist.prerequisite: KYC vendor; tax-form collection; sanctions screening
checklist.notes: Gift-card payout (Tremendous, Tango) is sometimes used to sidestep money-transmitter analysis, but it does NOT help the gambling analysis — a gift card is still a 'prize of value' under Stripe's, Adyen's and Apple's wording and under every state gambling statute's 'thing of value' element. It also creates a fresh escheatment obligation on the unredeemed card. Treat it as a convenience, not a legal structure.

headline: On the payments layer the four models split two-and-two and the split is absolute, not a matter of degree: Models A and D are ordinary digital-goods commerce that Stripe, Apple and Google will all serve today, while Models B and C are both inside Stripe's PROHIBITED column — Stripe's list names "Payments of an entry or player fee that promise the entrant or player will win a prize of value", which is a verbatim description of Model C — so the paid-entry skill contest is just as unbankable on mainstream rails as the sweepstakes casino, and the founder's likely assumption that "skill contest" is the safe middle path is wrong at the payments layer even where it may be right at the gambling-law layer.
jurisdiction: USA, EU and India — payments acceptance, money transmission, KYC/AML, age assurance and tax-reporting layer (cross-cutting)

modelVerdicts.authority: Stripe Prohibited and Restricted Businesses, last updated 13 May 2026 (fetched) — Model A appears on neither list. FinCEN Guidance FIN-2013-G001, 18 March 2013 (fetched): a non-convertible virtual currency has no "equivalent value in real currency" and does not "act as a substitute for real currency", so its issuer is not an administrator of CVC and not a money transmitter; "A user who obtains convertible virtual currency and uses it to purchase real or virtual goods or services is not an MSB". Apple App Store Review Guideline 3.1.1 (fetched). Google Play Payments policy (fetched): Play billing required for "Digital items (such as virtual currencies...)".
modelVerdicts.reasoning: Lawful, and fully served by mainstream rails. Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing all accept this as ordinary digital-goods commerce; it is how every free-to-play game on earth monetises. No money transmission arises because the coin is not convertible virtual currency — it has no real-currency equivalent and cannot substitute for currency. No gambling analysis arises because nothing is staked player-versus-player and nothing of value is won. Three payment-layer caveats that are easy to trip: (1) Paddle and Lemon Squeezy are NOT available even for Model A — Paddle's AUP (13 April 2026) prohibits "Virtual currency or stored value, including but not limited to store credit, gift cards, vouchers" outright; (2) Apple 3.1.1 forbids expiring IAP-purchased currency, so coin balances cannot be time-limited; (3) the Texas, Utah and Louisiana App Store Accountability Acts require parental consent for in-app purchases by minors, which reaches Model A even though nothing is gambled. The verdict flips the instant a single redemption path is added — one cash-out button converts the coin into CVC and pulls in FinCEN registration plus state MTLs.

modelVerdicts.authority: Stripe Prohibited and Restricted Businesses, 13 May 2026 (fetched), PROHIBITED: "Games of chance including gambling, internet gambling, casino games, sweepstakes and contests, and fantasy sports leagues with a monetary or material prize". Apple App Store Review Guideline 5.3.3 (fetched): "Apps may not use in-app purchase to purchase credit or currency for use in conjunction with real money gaming of any kind"; 5.3.4 requires licensing, geo-restriction and a free app. Google Play Real-Money Gambling, Games, and Contests policy (fetched): licensed operators only; app must be free, must not use Google Play In-app Billing, must block minors and unlicensed geographies, must be rated AO. Adyen Prohibited and Restricted list, 13 Nov 2025 (fetched): "Any type of US based gambling services" = PROHIBITED. FinCEN FIN-2013-G001 (fetched) on administrators of CVC. 31 CFR 1022.320 (fetched): SAR at $2,000, 30 days, 5-year retention. Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 (India, Act No. 32 of 2025, assent 22 August 2025).
modelVerdicts.reasoning: Licence-required, and on the payments layer effectively unbankable at seed stage. Three independent gates each of which alone blocks launch. (1) Acceptance: Stripe prohibits it with no pre-approval path and states it does not support gambling "regardless of local legality"; PayPal requires pre-approval conditioned on blocking US account holders; Paddle prohibits it twice over; Adyen will consider a waiver for a licensed EU/UK operator but prohibits US-based gambling services outright. That leaves only licence-gated specialist acquirers, which will not onboard you until you already hold the licence. (2) Money transmission: redeemable coins are convertible virtual currency and you become its administrator, which makes you a FinCEN-registered money transmitter needing a written AML programme, SAR filing at the $2,000 threshold within 30 days, and state MTLs. Note you do NOT get the friendlier casino rules — 31 CFR 1010.100(t) limits "casino" to duly licensed establishments with over $1m gross annual gaming revenue, so an unlicensed sweepstakes operator lands in the stricter MSB regime. (3) Store policy: Apple 5.3.3 forbids funding the stake through IAP at all, so on iOS the app must be free, licensed, geofenced and funded by an off-app web top-up; Google Play requires a per-jurisdiction gambling licence and forbids Play Billing. India is a flat no — the 2025 Act bans online money games whether of skill or chance and bars payment intermediaries from processing for them, so the offence sits on the payment aggregator as well as on you, meaning no Indian PA will onboard the merchant at any price.

modelVerdicts.authority: Stripe Prohibited and Restricted Businesses, 13 May 2026 (fetched), PROHIBITED: "Payments of an entry or player fee that promise the entrant or player will win a prize of value" and "Games of skill including video game and mobile game tournaments or competitions, darts, card games, and board games with a monetary or material prize". Adyen list, 13 Nov 2025 (fetched): "Legal gambling or Game of Skill where participants receive cash or cash equivalents or prizes with/of material value" = RESTRICTED (waiver) for merchants, PROHIBITED for platform/partner. Paddle AUP, 13 April 2026 (fetched): prohibits "Betting-related products, competition/event tickets, or entries". Apple Guidelines 5.3.1 and 5.3.2 (fetched). IRS Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754, rev. 01/2026 (fetched).
modelVerdicts.reasoning: Genuinely unsettled at the payments layer, and much harder than the founder will expect — this is the finding most likely to change the plan. The fixed-and-pre-announced prize pool is the classic structure for taking a contest outside gambling law, because the prize does not depend on the stakes of other entrants. But payment processors do not apply gambling law; they apply their own category lists, and Stripe's list names this structure explicitly and puts it in the PROHIBITED column, not the restricted one. Adyen is more workable — it classes "Game of Skill" as restricted-with-waiver for direct merchants, so a licensed or clearly-lawful EU operator has a route, though Adyen's blanket prohibition on US-based gambling services and its prohibition for platform/partner businesses narrow it sharply. Apple will host it under 5.3.1 and 5.3.2 (the developer must sponsor the contest and publish official rules stating Apple is not a sponsor), which is a meaningfully lighter regime than 5.3.4. Google Play is the risk: its policy prohibits unlicensed apps that let users "wager, stake, or participate using real money... to obtain a prize of real world monetary value", and a fixed-pool skill contest arguably falls inside "participate using real money to obtain a prize of real world monetary value". India bans it regardless — the 2025 Act covers games of skill expressly. Payouts still drag in the full KYC, sanctions-screening, W-9/W-8BEN, 1099-MISC (threshold now $2,000 from 2026) and escheatment stack, none of which the fixed-prize structure avoids.

modelVerdicts.authority: Stripe Prohibited and Restricted Businesses, 13 May 2026 (fetched) — subscriptions for features and cosmetics appear on neither list. Paddle AUP, 13 April 2026 (fetched) — software subscriptions are Paddle's core permitted category. Apple App Store Review Guideline 3.1.1 (fetched). Google Play Payments policy (fetched). Texas, Utah and Louisiana App Store Accountability Acts (secondary: Wiley, Morrison Foerster, McNees).
modelVerdicts.reasoning: Lawful and the cleanest model on every payments dimension. No stake, no prize of value, no convertible currency, therefore no gambling analysis, no money transmission, no KYC/AML, no 1099 and no escheatment. Every rail is open including the merchant-of-record route, which is genuinely useful here: a MoR such as Paddle or FastSpring absorbs global VAT/GST registration and remittance, chargeback liability and PCI merchant scope for a subscription business, and unlike in Models B and C there is no payout half for the MoR to fail to cover. Requirements reduce to: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing for the in-app path; SAQ A via hosted fields for a web path; honour the app-store age signal so a minor's subscription gets parental consent in Texas, Utah and Louisiana; and standard auto-renewal disclosure and cancellation law (US FTC negative-option rules and the EU consumer acquis — outside this lane, flag to counsel).

risks: The single biggest payments risk is misdescribing the business at onboarding. Every processor agreement makes a prohibited-business breach grounds for immediate termination, fund freeze for 90-180 days, a rolling reserve, and MATCH/TMF listing — which blacklists the principals, not just the company, across effectively all acquirers for five years. A founder who onboards Model B or C to Stripe as a 'trivia game' and is caught later is not back at square one, they are behind it.

Stripe's PROHIBITED line 'Payments of an entry or player fee that promise the entrant or player will win a prize of value' describes Model C exactly. Any plan that assumes the fixed-prize skill contest is the safe commercial middle path needs to be re-planned around Adyen or a specialist acquirer from the start, not discovered after building the checkout.

Merchant-of-record is likely to be over-trusted. It moves card-scheme liability, PCI scope and tax remittance; it does not move gambling licensing, money transmission, AML, age assurance, or the legality of the stake — and no MoR does payouts at all, so for Models B and C the MoR covers only the easy half.

The current live product already stakes 'coins' into an 'escrow' where 'the winner takes the escrow'. That language is shipped, public at the GitHub Pages URL, and indexable. Underwriters read the live site. It should be neutralised before any merchant application is filed, regardless of which model is eventually chosen.

Apple 5.3.3 forbids buying stake currency via IAP for real-money gaming of any kind. Model B on iOS therefore cannot use the obvious funding mechanism and must route users to a web top-up — which is workable on the US storefront (3.1.1(a) now exempts US-storefront apps from the anti-steering prohibition) but needs a StoreKit External Purchase Link Entitlement elsewhere, and the US carve-out rests on litigation that can move.

Apple requires Play-style virtual currency via IAP while Google Play forbids Play Billing in licensed real-money gambling apps. The two store policies do not compose for Model B — that incompatibility is itself the signal that Model B is not a store-native product anywhere.

India is not a market for Models B or C at any price. The 2025 Act places the payment-facilitation offence on the bank and the payment aggregator as well as on the operator, so the refusal comes from the rail, not from a risk committee that might be persuaded.

Escheatment is the commonly missed obligation and it accrues silently. Dormant cash-redeemable balances become state unclaimed property after a dormancy period of roughly one to five years depending on the state, and the holder's state of incorporation is the fallback claimant for address-unknown owners. If last-activity timestamps are not recorded from day one, the liability cannot be computed later and an audit assessment is estimated against you.

A single-integer 'coins' field that mixes purchased, granted and won value makes it impossible to answer the one question every processor, regulator and auditor asks: can purchased value become withdrawable value? Splitting the ledger is a cheap design decision now and a data-migration nightmare after launch.

Biometric selfie matching for KYC triggers Illinois BIPA (statutory damages per violation, private right of action) and Texas CUBI. This is a real litigation risk that is separate from, and can exceed, the gambling risk.
The 24% backup withholding on a payout to a user with no TIN on file is unrecoverable from the user once paid. Collect W-9/W-8BEN before the first payout, not at year end.

PCI DSS v4.0.1's April 2025 SAQ A eligibility criteria now require confirming the payment page is not susceptible to script attacks. FACT//DUEL is a script-heavy React and three.js app, which is exactly the Magecart target profile. Script inventory, subresource integrity and CSP on the checkout page are load-bearing for keeping SAQ A eligibility.

Regulatory currency risk in this research itself: eur-lex.europa.eu, ecfr.gov, ofcom.org.uk, meity.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in were all unreachable from this environment, so the EU AMLR thresholds, the CTR rules, the UK OSA age-assurance duties and the Indian Act's section numbers rest on secondary sources and are flagged UNVERIFIED throughout. Do not let any of those propagate into a filing.

subdivisions.authority: Texas App Store Accountability Act (SB 2420); preliminary injunction stayed by the US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit — secondary: Morrison Foerster alert, Nov 2025
subdivisions.detail: Effective 1 January 2026. App stores must verify age at account creation and bracket users under-13 / 13-15 / 16-17 / 18+; parental consent required for app downloads, app purchases and in-app purchases. Developer-side duty is to receive and act on the store's age signal. Applies to Models A and D as well, because coin and subscription purchases by minors need consent. UNVERIFIED: current litigation posture — verify before relying on either the law being in force or enjoined.
subdivisions.name: Texas (age assurance)

subdivisions.authority: Utah App Store Accountability Act — secondary: Wiley, McNees, Baker Data Counsel
subdivisions.detail: Developer and provider obligations effective 6 May 2026; private right of action enforceable from 31 December 2026. Same age-bracketing and parental-consent architecture as Texas. The private right of action is the material risk — it removes reliance on regulator discretion.
subdivisions.name: Utah (age assurance)

subdivisions.authority: Louisiana App Store Accountability Act — secondary: Wiley, McNees
subdivisions.detail: Effective 1 July 2026. Same age-verification-at-account-creation and parental-consent-for-in-app-purchase structure.
subdivisions.name: Louisiana (age assurance)

subdivisions.authority: Virginia Money Transmission Modernization Act, effective 1 July 2026 — secondary: Shipkevich, CryptoSlate analyses
subdivisions.detail: Enacts the CSBS MTMA. Defines 'money' to exclude virtual currency, and the virtual-currency definition itself reportedly excludes certain merchant-rewards value and game-platform value. If a non-redeemable game coin sits inside that exclusion, Model A needs no Virginia licence. Model B's redeemable coin almost certainly falls outside it. UNVERIFIED: exact statutory wording of the game-platform exclusion was not fetched — this is the highest-value item for counsel to pin down, because the same carve-out language recurs across the 31 MTMA states.
subdivisions.name: Virginia (money transmission)

subdivisions.authority: CSBS MTMA optional virtual-currency provisions — secondary: FinTech and Blockchain Law Watch, May 2025
subdivisions.detail: Reported as the only two states to have enacted the MTMA's optional virtual-currency business-activity provisions, which require a money transmitter licence for virtual-currency business activity. Model B should assume licence-required here even if other MTMA states' game-platform exclusions apply.
subdivisions.name: North Dakota and Minnesota (virtual-currency money transmission)

subdivisions.authority: New York Financial Services Law / 23 NYCRR Part 200 (BitLicense) — NOT verified in this research
subdivisions.detail: UNVERIFIED. New York historically sits outside the MTMA consensus and runs its own virtual-currency regime alongside its money transmitter licence. Any redeemable-coin model must get a specific New York opinion before accepting New York users; do not assume the MTMA game-platform carve-out reaches here.
subdivisions.name: New York (money transmission / virtual currency)

subdivisions.authority: Delaware Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act; the incorporation-state fallback priority rule derives from Texas v. New Jersey (1965) — the case was NOT verified in this research
subdivisions.detail: UNVERIFIED but structurally important. Unclaimed property generally escheats to the state of the owner's last known address, and where no address is known, to the holder's state of incorporation. A Delaware-incorporated startup therefore pulls every address-unknown dormant balance into Delaware's regime, which is the most aggressively audited in the country. Relevant to Models B and C, and to Model A only if coins are ever refundable.
subdivisions.name: Delaware (escheatment — holder domicile)

subdivisions.authority: Colorado Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act — secondary: Baker Tilly, EisnerAmper
subdivisions.detail: Colorado's RUUPA expressly encompasses stored-value cards including gift cards, so the unused monetary value held by the issuer is subject to the Act. Illustrates the general pattern: a cash-redeemable user balance is reportable unclaimed property after the dormancy period (typically one to five years, state-dependent). A genuinely non-redeemable Model A coin is arguably not property at all — another reason to keep the closed loop closed.
subdivisions.name: Colorado (escheatment — stored value)

subdivisions.authority: Adyen Prohibited and Restricted Products and Services List, last updated 13 November 2025 (fetched)
subdivisions.detail: 'Any type of US based gambling services' sits in Adyen's PROHIBITED column with no waiver route, while 'Legal gambling or Game of Skill where participants receive cash or cash equivalents or prizes with/of material value' is merely RESTRICTED (written waiver, revocable at Adyen's sole discretion) for direct merchants and PROHIBITED for platform/partner businesses. Net effect on strategy: Adyen is a viable EU/UK acquirer for Models B and C but cannot be the US rail, so a US launch needs a separate specialist acquirer.
subdivisions.name: EU and UK vs United States (Adyen acceptance)

subdivisions.authority: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2) Article 3(k) and the EBA Guidelines on the limited network exclusion; national competent authorities
subdivisions.detail: Authorisation as an EMI or payment institution is a single-member-state application that passports across the EEA, so unlike US state MTLs this is one process not twenty-seven. The dividing line is cash-out: secondary commentary is consistent that an instrument relying on the limited network exclusion must not permit cash-out, which maps exactly onto the Model A / Model B boundary. UNVERIFIED: EBA Guidelines text, LNE notification thresholds, and per-state initial capital and fees were not fetched. Also note PSD3/PSR reportedly reached provisional agreement 27 November 2025 and would merge the PI and EMI regimes, with application around 2027 — apply under the current framework and expect grandfathering.
subdivisions.name: EU member states generally (EMI / payment institution passporting)

subdivisions.authority: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 (Act No. 32 of 2025), assent 22 August 2025; Rules notified 22 April 2026 (secondary: Wikipedia, PIB)
subdivisions.detail: Prohibited for Models B and C, permitted for Models A and D. The Act bans all online money games whether of chance, skill or a combination, and — per law-firm summaries, reported as section 7, UNVERIFIED — bars banks, financial institutions, payment aggregators, gateways, wallet operators and card networks from facilitating any transaction toward an online money gaming service. Because the offence attaches to the payment intermediary as well as the operator, there is no commercial workaround: the RBI-authorised PA refuses as a matter of its own criminal exposure. 'Online social games' and e-sports are expressly promoted, which is where Models A and D sit. Google's earlier India real-money-gaming pilot for daily fantasy sports and rummy is superseded.
subdivisions.name: India (nationwide — payment facilitation ban)

uncertain: EU AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624: no article number, EUR customer-due-diligence threshold for gambling, member-state low-risk exemption, or date of application is asserted. eur-lex.europa.eu returned empty responses across four separate fetch attempts (HTML, PDF, CELEX and ELI URL forms) and the environment's proxy would not relay it. Everything about AMLR in this report is a statement of what counsel must find, not a finding.

India, Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025: the section numbers (reported as sections 5, 6 and 7 for the offering, advertising and financial-transaction prohibitions), the penalty amounts (reported as up to 3 years imprisonment and INR 1 crore) and the commencement date all come from secondary sources — Trilegal, PIB press releases and Wikipedia. meity.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in both returned HTTP 403, and ogai.gov.in was refused by the proxy gateway. The substance — a total ban on online money games including skill games, plus a payment-facilitation prohibition — is corroborated across independent sources and is safe to plan around; the citations are not safe to file.

31 CFR 1010.311 and 1010.306 (Currency Transaction Report threshold and filing deadline) were not verified. ecfr.gov redirects to an unblock page from this environment. The $10,000 figure is well known but is not asserted here as verified, and CTR applicability to a card-funded online game is genuinely doubtful since CTRs attach to currency.

31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(8): the $1,000-per-person-per-day de minimis that applies to most MSB categories and its reported non-application to money transmitters could not be confirmed. The Cornell fetch did not surface it. If a money transmitter has no de minimis — which is the conventional understanding — then even a single small redeemable payout creates MSB status, which is a material planning fact. Confirm before relying on it.

The CSBS MTMA's definition of 'money' and the game-platform / merchant-rewards exclusion within its virtual-currency definition were confirmed only through secondary analyses of Virginia's enactment. The actual model-law text was not fetched. This is the single most valuable item to verify because it determines whether Model A needs any state licence at all.

UK Online Safety Act 2023: 'highly effective age assurance', the commencing duties, the in-force date and whether licensed gambling is carved out to the Gambling Commission's LCCP instead were all unverified — ofcom.org.uk returned HTTP 403. The commonly cited 25 July 2025 commencement for HEAA duties is not asserted here.

EU Digital Services Act Article 28 minor-protection duties and the Commission's 2025 guidelines on protection of minors were not researched at all; the web-search budget was exhausted before reaching them. Age assurance expectations in the EU are therefore a gap in this report.

Published per-verification pricing for Persona, Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido and Jumio could not be obtained from vendor sites — withpersona.com/pricing and veriff.com/product/pricing returned 403 and 404 respectively. The indicative $0.80-$5.00 range comes from low-quality SEO comparison blogs and should be treated as worthless for budgeting. Only Stripe Identity's $1.50 document-and-selfie and $0.50 ID-number-lookup prices were verified from stripe.com/pricing.

Apple's current commission rates (standard, Small Business Program, and the US external-purchase-link rate) and Google Play's base service fee were not verified; only Play's India/South Korea 4-percentage-point alternative-billing reduction was confirmed from the Payments policy.

Card-network treatment was not researched: MCC 7995 assignment rules, Visa's and Mastercard's high-integrity-risk or high-brand-risk merchant registration programmes, their registration fees and their required transaction-coding are all unverified. These are a real and significant cost line for Models B and C and need to come from the prospective acquirer.

Lead times and fees for state money transmitter licences, EMI authorisation, and gambling-specialist PSP onboarding are all UNVERIFIED. Historically a broad US MTL footprint is a multi-year, seven-figure programme, but no current figure is asserted.

Whether a Model C fixed-prize skill contest entry fee constitutes a 'wager' for IRS purposes — determining Form W-2G versus Form 1099-MISC Box 3 treatment — is unresolved. The Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754 (rev. 01/2026) address gambling winnings only and are silent on skill contests. This needs a tax opinion, not a search result.
Texas v. New Jersey (1965) and the unclaimed-property priority rules were not verified in this research; the incorporation-state fallback is stated from general knowledge and flagged accordingly.

PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation: the reported 27 November 2025 provisional political agreement, publication in the Official Journal in H1 2026, and application around 2027 are from a single secondary commercial source and were not corroborated against Council or Parliament materials.

RBI Payment Aggregator directions: the current merchant-onboarding rules and prohibited-category list were not fetched. Whether an Indian PA will onboard a non-redeemable in-game coin post-Act is an assumption, not a finding.

This is a compliance checklist assembled from public sources, not legal advice. Models B and C require licensed gambling/gaming counsel in each target jurisdiction plus US money-transmission counsel before any merchant application is filed. Model A needs a short opinion on the MTMA game-platform exclusion and on whether the coin is 'property' for escheatment. Model D needs only routine auto-renewal and consumer-law review.
